description.narrative:
NWPC’s adopted new approach of combining the e-learning portal and online coaching for MSMEs to provide uninterrupted advisory services to support enterprises towards recovery.
ECOP created the Diversity and Inclusion Committee for the development of policy and programme initatives to promote the welfare and advancement of women in the workplace and women entrepreneurs (August 2021)
560 women trained in Soft Skills Training for Industry Associations and Companies (September 2021)
78 women entrepreneurs trained in Canva for Marketing your Business for Women Entrepreneurs under ILO Rebuilding Better Project
Localized online training program on Business Continuity Planning and Management for enterprise resilience was developed by the NWPC based on the ILO training materials and content.
Tools (ILO and others) and advisory service models to support enterprise 'green' upskilling, recovery and resilience (InSIGHT2)
Online In-Business Soft Skills Training for Women provided to SMEs (STEM)
TOT workshops conducted for the training institutions on the ILO tools that support MSMEs to become more productive and sustainable in the increasingly digitalizing economy in the context of human-centred recovery from the COVID-19 crisis. (Japan MSME)
Innovative advisory service models to support enterprises in upskilling/green HRD, green recovery and resilience in partnership with key constituents (ie NWPC's e-learning portal and coaching for MSMEs) (InSIGHT2)

Output 4.4. Increased capacity of member States and enterprises to develop policies and measures that promote the alignment of business practices with decent work and a human-centred approach to the future of work

description.narrative:
The Philippine Fruit Industry utilize the ILO studies on socially responsible labour practices and the labour aspect of RBC/CSR as input to the tripartite dialogue on CSR.
93 HR Offices of selected industry associations have been trained to ensure sustainability of implementation of CSR training among their members
302 enterprises (composed and SMES and MNEs) have increased knowledge and understanding of CSR/RBC, international CSR frameworks, ILS and model CSR cases
158 future business have better knowledge and understanding on the importance of their role in the transformation of business practices to being more socially responsible
Policy makers were made more aware of the comprehensive scope of CSR through the Technical Webinar titled “Corporate Social Responsibility/Responsible Business Conduct for Policymakers, The Contribution of Socially Responsible Labour Practices to the Achievement of Sustainable Development in the Philippines”. Evidence created on DW challenges in the fruit commodity sector through an integrative analysis of ILO studies on pineapple, coconut and banana (RSCA)
Decent work challenges mapped out and good practices on CSR/RBC in the banana sector identified through the study on fruit and vegetable supply and CSR/RBC for social and economic upgrading (RSCA)
Greater awareness created among 200 representatives from government, enterprises and workers on the role and importance of CSR/RBC in times of COVID19 through a technical webinar on CSR/RBC.
Tripartite Action Plan developed on the promotion on CSR/RBC practices as an output of the Tripartite Plus Dialogue on CSR/RBC (RSCA)
Capacity developed among 70 HR Officers of selected industry associations on implementation of CSR training among their members (RSCA)
Increased knowledge and understanding of about 250 enterprises on CSR/RBC, international CSR frameworks, ILS and model CSR cases (RSCA)
Better knowledge and understanding created among 170 future business leaders on the importance of their role in the transformation of business practices into being more socially responsible. (RSCA)
Better understanding of policy makers on the comprehsive scope of CSR and their important role in developing a national framework that would set the standards to guide and encourage businesses to initiate or improve their CSR performance. (RSCA)
